title: Fixed-prefix pairing in linear time and constant space
statement: For every fixed Boolean word $\alpha$, there are a finite Turing machine $M$ and a constant $c\in\mathbb{N}$ such that, on every Boolean input $x$, $M$ halts within $c(|x|+1)$ steps and outputs the pairing of $\alpha$ with $x$. At every time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, the computation of $M$ on any input uses at most $c$ work-tape cells.
